oh_workout_wall.blurb: A small boulder cluster along the cliff line in Hocking Hills State Forest, reached by continuing along the trail beyond Sunshine Valley and climbing a short hill. Roughly a dozen lines, nearly all of them boulder problems, with a single top rope on the right side of the wall. Difficulty mostly sits between V0 and V2, with a few V3 and V4 problems for stronger climbers, and the top rope is around 5.8. An overhanging section holds most of the problems, plus one freestanding boulder in front of the cliff. The spot is open and catches more sun than the other nearby bouldering areas, making it a decent warm-up stop.

oh_front_wall.blurb: A boulder wall in Mill Creek MetroParks near Youngstown, tucked behind the Bears Den cabin where an old quarry has become a stream and scattered boulders. Every one of the dozen lines is a bouldering problem, with most falling between V1 and V3 and a handful of harder ones reaching V4 and beyond. The wall sits out of the sun, so holds can be grimy, and the sandstone is mossy in places. Landings are clear but can turn muddy, and topping out is best avoided. It is a handy stop for a session alongside the neighbouring Squid Wall and Fault Line boulders.

oh_south_wall_3.blurb: A wall at Kiedaisch Point, a hillside crag above the Ohio River near the Hannibal and New Martinsville bridge. The dozen or so routes are split between bolted lines and gear routes, with the sport side a little bigger. Grades run from very easy 5.3 and 5.4 trad lines up through the 5.10s, with a lone 5.11 for the keen. The setting is a shaded hillside with an easy walk up from the road, so it suits beginners starting on the gentler gear routes and easy bolted lines, while stronger climbers can find a few harder sport pitches.

oh_lorax_wall.blurb: The tallest section of the small quarry at West Branch State Park, easy to reach on foot from the parking lot. Most of the twelve lines are short top ropes with a gentle tone, ranging from 5.3 through the 5.8 range, plus one hard 5.11 for those who want a challenge and a pair of V2 boulder problems along the base. The area is mostly shaded while the trees are in leaf, and the quarry works well for beginners. A bike trail runs along the clifftop, so keep an eye out for riders when setting up from above.

oh_mollies_rock.blurb: A steep sandstone wall of roughly 45 feet in the Tri-Valley Wildlife Area, near Zanesville. It began as a spot for bouldering and top roping and has since been turned toward sport climbing, with around ten bolted lines plus a few boulder problems. Most of the roped climbs sit in the 5.9 to 5.12 range, with a good cluster in the 5.11s and a couple of 5.12s, so it suits intermediate to strong leaders. The wall is mostly overhanging, usually shaded and quick to dry, and one reachy moderate line is the most popular on the crag.

oh_c_warm_up_wall.blurb: The first wall you meet on the Marne Road cliff line near Hanover, offering a dozen mostly bolted routes of about 30 feet with a single trad line. Grades cluster around 5.9 with a spread from 5.7 up to a 5.11, so it works well as a warm-up or as a base for climbers working through the moderates. Climbing is on highly featured sandstone that is crumbly in spots, with some blank stretches, and a damp mossy chimney sits in the middle. Most lines dry quickly after rain, although a pocket or ledge may stay wet.

oh_harmony_boulders.blurb: A short overhanging stretch on the left end of the Harmony Wall cliff, in the Harmony Trail area of Paint Creek State Park in southwest Ohio. About a dozen boulder problems, spread from V0 up to V6, with a couple of each grade in the middle and upper range. The dolomite is solid and the cliff is shady all day, though holds can be a little dirty. The collection is small and not highly rated, but a few problems are hard, and it sees very little traffic. Reach it by following the trail to the wall and walking left.
